data.narrative:
Kinetic Automation is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Nikhil Naikal and Sander Marques, having raised approximately $31M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $31M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $59M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against three same-sector, same-stage private companies with valuations ranging from $1.6B to $2.0B, producing a median implied value of $1.8B.

The divergence between methods reflects material uncertainty inherent in early-stage frontier tech valuation. The stage-progression floor of $50M assumes funding velocity and dilution patterns; the peer-median ceiling of $2.0B anchors to observable market pricing for robotics startups at equivalent maturity. A triangulated range of $50M to $2.0B emerges, with median at $904M. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, pathway to differentiation in a competitive cohort, and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable revenue models or speculative positioning in the sector.
